Flowline follows Hydro Modify in the Study workspace. Its linked Survey Event
selector supports every locally defined Event and stays synchronized with the
other terrain tabs. Opening the tab uses the selected Event and Stream, reads the exact saved Hydro
revision and synthetic Stream Network candidate, and selects one raw Stream-level
path without asking the analyst to choose network heads or segments. Stream
definition already records that intent.

## From the tab to Reach Flowlines

`flowline_review_server()` resolves the saved inputs through
`hydro_read()`, `stream_network_read()` and `stream_segments()`. The ordinary
`load_flowline_review()` adapter first reopens an exact saved Flowline candidate.
Only when none exists does it read `stream-network.gpkg` and call
`fluvgeo::select_stream_mainstem()`. The backend validates a one-outlet acyclic
directed tree, enumerates every complete head-to-outlet route and compares each
full terrain path with the retained NHDPlusV2 Stream geometry using discrete
Hausdorff distance. Among equivalent best reference matches it selects the
longest route; stable upstream-cell ordering resolves a remaining exact tie.
Reference geometry identifies the selected Stream but never supplies output
coordinates.

The selection result includes one downstream-to-upstream raw `sf` line, the
ordered source `stream_line_id` rows and every candidate route with length, reference mismatch,
rank and selection flags. `derive_reach_flowlines()` projects the ordered retained
Reach transitions onto the raw path, transfers them to the selected smoothed path,
and passes each divided line through the existing `fluvgeo::flowline()` contract
with its Reach name. Its explicit topology-preserving mode keeps known network
direction; the historical DEM-oriented default and arbitrary browser-drawn lines
used by `{ohwm2}` are unchanged. `smooth_flowline()` applies Gaussian kernel regression at
the requested 2, 3, 4 or 5 map-unit bandwidth, with fixed endpoints, simple/valid
geometry checks and a maximum-displacement guard equal to that bandwidth. The conservative
2-map-unit candidate remains the default. Other strengths are prepared lazily
and cached for the session. This portable method is not claimed to
reproduce PAEK vertices.

The complete call and data path is:

1. selecting the **Flowline** tab or another Stream checks a cheap Event/Stream
   session key before any file access; an unchanged binding reuses the prepared
   review, while a changed binding calls `load_flowline_review()`;
2. the adapter uses `hydro_read()`, `stream_network_read()` and
   `stream_segments()` to resolve the exact Hydro DEM, network, reference lines,
   Reach mappings and Reach inventory;
3. `select_stream_mainstem()`, `smooth_flowline()` and
   `derive_reach_flowlines()` perform the reusable scientific work in
   `{fluvgeo}`; and
4. the conservative default, or an explicit smoothing change, automatically
   calls the store's `flowline_publish()` closure. `study_flowline_store()`
   writes and rereads the completed revision.

The app map displays the selected and smoothed path in gold, the complete synthetic
network in muted cyan and saved NHDPlusV2 evidence in dashed magenta over the
same viewport-stretched Hydro DEM and hillshade used for terrain review. The
map fits the full saved Stream with a small margin whenever its Stream tab is
selected or the workflow tab becomes visible, while ordinary visible-map resizes
preserve analyst zoom and pan. OpenTopoMap is the default basemap. The
summary reports the routes evaluated, source-line count, path length, reference
mismatch, next-best reference margin and smoothing diagnostics. There is no
manual branch control. The analyst can switch among four available smoothing
strengths without rerunning mainstem selection or terrain processing; each is
computed only on first use, saved automatically, and then cached. The selected
gold line, Reach divisions and diagnostics update immediately. Colored lines
show one candidate per Reach and white points show exact shared endpoints. The
smoothing selection publishes the chosen result as a local immutable revision. The
viewport-stretched elevation display is prepared asynchronously from the saved
GeoTIFF and is regenerable; it never modifies analytical terrain. Missing Hydro
or network prerequisites route the analyst back to Hydro Modify. Invalid network
topology, unsupported Reach mappings, ambiguous boundary projections and changed
inputs fail explicitly instead of inventing geometry or silently reusing stale
work.

## Local completion and governance boundary

The screen completes local Flowline creation. A saved candidate contains one
continuous downstream-to-upstream line per current Reach plus the common raw and
smoothed Stream paths, selected network segments and boundary evidence. It reopens
only while the Study context, Survey Event setting, Hydro revision, synthetic
network, retained reference and Reach mapping fingerprints remain exact. A changed
input leaves the prior immutable directory intact but excludes it from current
review. On reopen, the newest exact matching revision is loaded and its smoothing
bandwidth is selected. Choosing another bandwidth prepares, validates, and saves
another immutable revision automatically rather than changing the old one.
Enterprise publication and governed Reach-owned Survey Event/Dataset
Edition identities remain a later boundary and are not required for the local
Flowline Points workflow.

| Data object / preparation asset | Operation | Storage and ownership |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Saved Hydro DEM revision | `hydro_read()` | Existing Hydro-revision external GeoTIFF; read-only |
| Synthetic Stream Network revision | `stream_network_read()` | Existing Hydro-revision-local `stream-network.gpkg`; read-only |
| Retained NHDPlusV2 Stream evidence | `stream_segments()` | Hash-linked Stream selection/piece GeoPackage; read-only reference evidence |
| Automatically selected Stream path | `select_stream_mainstem()` then `smooth_flowline()` at 2–5 map units | Transient raw path, candidate scores and four smoothed `sf` previews; only the chosen smoothing is saved |
| Reach Flowline candidates | `derive_reach_flowlines()` and `study_flowline_store()` | Immutable network-revision-local `flowline/<revision>/flowlines.gpkg`, `result.rds` and `provenance.json`; local preparation product, not governed FGDB acceptance |
| Viewport elevation/hillshade | `prepare_hydro_dem_view()` | Regenerable session display from the Hydro GeoTIFF; analytical terrain is unchanged |

`flowlines.gpkg` contains `raw_stream_flowline`, `smoothed_stream_flowline`,
internal `reach_flowlines`, legacy-compatible `flowline`, and
`selected_network_segments`; `reach_boundaries` is present
when the Stream has more than one Reach. The result index and matching JSON record
the schema, selected bandwidth, Reach IDs, timestamp, GeoPackage hash and exact
input fingerprint. That fingerprint covers the Study context and event-setting
files, Hydro revision/output hash, network revision/GeoPackage hash, retained
reference hash and serialized Reach-mapping hash. A `PENDING` marker prevents an
incomplete directory from being treated as published. The store verifies the
GeoPackage hash and required layers before returning a saved candidate.

The `flowline` layer preserves the legacy production fields `ReachName`,
`from_measure`, and `to_measure`; measures are continuous kilometres upstream
from the selected Stream outlet. Modern Reach identity, order and explicit
length fields are additive. These are local candidate measures until a governed
FGDB longitudinal frame and calibration exist. Older local candidate revisions
without the compatibility layer remain readable and receive the same fields in
memory; they are not rewritten.

The GeoPackage features retain selection, smoothing, direction and source-line
attributes produced by the backend. The local result index does not create
governed `flowline_id`, `survey_event_id`, Dataset Edition or acceptance records,
and it does not preserve every unsaved alternative route or smoothing candidate.
Those distinctions prevent local preparation evidence from being mistaken for
the draft normalized FGDB Flowline contract while retaining the required legacy
producer schema. See the legacy-derived-feature compatibility workflow and FGDB
profile before changing this layer.

## Verification and maintenance routes

Verification starts with `test-flowline-review.R` and `test-flowline-store.R` in
FG Studio and `test_select_stream_mainstem.R`, `test_smooth_flowline.R`,
`test_flowline_reaches.R` plus `test_flowline.R` in `{fluvgeo}`. Real Spencer
integration produces five mainstem, three east-tributary and three west-tributary
Reach Flowlines, with four, two and two exact shared boundaries respectively.
These real-data counts verify the current Study configuration; they are not a
general qualification across terrain forms. If reopening fails, inspect
`R/flowline_store.R` and its fingerprints first. If selection or smoothing is
wrong, inspect the corresponding `{fluvgeo}` function and test. If Reach division
fails, inspect the retained `reach_mappings` and `derive_reach_flowlines()`.
Flowline Points consumes the saved candidate, not transient session geometry.
